hook_text: A basket on stilts, a pit sealed with clay, a jar of atchar. Three ways to beat the things that eat your food first.
clip_script: Food spoils because bacteria, moulds, weevils and rats eat it before you do. They need moisture, warmth, air and a way in. Take one away and the food keeps. Grain: dry it in sun and smoke, store it in a basket on stilts with rat collars, or seal it in a clay-capped pit where insects suffocate. Today it is a steel silo at 12 percent moisture, fans and a seal. Same four ideas: dry, cool, sealed, off the ground. Pickling: make it sour. Pour vinegar on it, or pack it in brine and let the good bacteria sour it until nothing else can live there. Keep everything under the liquid, jar clean and sealed.
visual_style: Whiteboard spoilers with their needs crossed out; a raised basket, a sealed pit and a silo side by side with four ticks; a jar with liquid line and a vegetable poking above it circled red.
mood: Practical and respectful of old knowledge.
pacing: Spoilers, deny, grain old, grain new, four ideas, vinegar, ferment, rules.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find out how maize meal is stored in your kitchen and whether it meets the four rules.
